title: Saved JSON export recipes for Open WebUI

reference.analysis: symbol-assisted binary inspection; no reference source supplied to the builder

input.records: Array of JSON objects; at most 10000 rows
input.columns: Array of 1..32 objects: label (nonempty string <=128 chars), path (array of 0..16 string or nonnegative integer segments), optional fallback (scalar), fallback_mode ('jq' default, or 'null')
input.fallback: Only applied if the column includes the fallback key. jq mode replaces null, missing, or false. null mode replaces only null or missing. Zero and empty string are preserved.
input.numbers: Only integers within +/-9007199254740991. Reject floating-point values and larger integers.

output.success: Object with columns (ordered labels), rows (ordered arrays of scalar values), csv (header + rows, LF after every row). Match jq @csv: strings always quoted, quotes doubled, null empty, booleans lowercase, integers decimal. Escape NUL inside strings as backslash followed by zero, as jq does.
output.error: Return only {'error': CODE}. Codes: invalid_recipe for malformed shapes or options; limit_exceeded for input/row/column bounds; unsupported_number for prohibited numbers anywhere in the request; path_type for incompatible path traversal; non_scalar for object/array result or fallback. Missing object keys and out-of-range array indexes return null. Traversal through null returns null. Do not raise exceptions for JSON input.

acceptance: Agent writes and runs focused unittest cases before delivery
Separate evaluator compares valid requests with the pinned jq binary
Independent invalid-input checks enforce the contract
Candidate has no subprocess, network, file IO, imports outside the approved stdlib set, or dynamic code execution
GitHub CI succeeds for the exact delivered commit
An authorized Open WebUI upload produces a CSV and a saved recipe works after reload
